key_gap: The AI independently identified the real need (dose-state verification and refill-week reconciliation, overriding the survey's stated 'bigger print, louder alarm' need) by reading the observation data as evidence in WHY — a strong result — but it selected the product form (mechanical taken-latch strip) without running the prototype-test-iterate loop. The human's v1 test with 5 seniors found the latch too stiff for arthritic hands (4/5 fail) — a failure reasoning alone could not predict — and wrote the v2 spec (slide, not pinch; larger dial) from that finding, then retested (5/5 pass). The AI logged the ergonomic question as open risk in its own AAR instead of resolving it by testing; its selected form carries the same unverified failure mode that caused abandonment of the existing pillbox.
learning_signal: For user-facing product recommendations, observation data can be read as evidence, but usability acceptance is an empirical question that only a prototype test answers. The design cycle's decisive move is not the insight — both sides reached it — it is the fail-and-iterate loop: test v1 with target users, let the observed failure rewrite the spec, retest. The AI's evidence-review pass stopped one step short of the empirical test that converts 'APPROXIMATED, ergonomics unverified' into a validated artifact; the untested latch is a discovery-by-reasoning failure in exactly the demographic (80+ hands) where the product lives.
suggested_improvement: Add a USER TEST GATE to the v5 process for any recommendation that is a user-facing artifact: in HOW selection, require (a) a defined low-fi prototype, (b) a stated test protocol with ≥3 target users, and (c) a recorded fail → iterate → retest cycle, OR the packet's status must degrade to NEEDS_EXPERIMENT/APPROXIMATED with the untested claim named in risks. Make the G-WHY or a new pre-DO gate check 'is any accepted claim answered only by reasoning when a cheap test exists?' — if yes, the test is part of the recommendation, not optional.

key_gap: Strict design thinking ran a genuine, full-cycle engagement (empathy → journey maps → clickable app + lobby prototypes) whose testing showed 10/12 residents loving the app and 'feeling in control' — and zero movement in the wait arithmetic, because the binding constraint (Car B out of service 30% of the year, 6-week repair backlog, 5-day SLA; two 25-person cars vs. a 300-person morning surge = ≥12 loads ≈ 6–8 min single-car) was present in the available logs and went unread. The call-ahead app adds zero cars and can lengthen real waits. The AI routed by constraint: capacity arithmetic before any empathy claim, the app rejected on physics, the fix built on expedited repair + SLA renegotiation + express bypass + group dispatch, with honest status signage as the one UX element that does real work — which was exactly the human's single late-arriving insight, subordinated where it belongs.
learning_signal: Design thinking's empiricism must be routed to the constraint surface, not the preference surface. User love of a prototype is evidence about preference, never about throughput: residents delighting in a call-ahead app is fully compatible with a hoist that cannot clear the surge. The corrective discipline is a pre-ideation constraint screen for physical/operational systems: identify the binding constraint (availability, capacity, SLA, physics), run the capacity arithmetic, and require every proposed solution to survive it — before any empathy work is spent. Where user truth and constraint align (residents want honest status; honest status also cuts phantom-car calls), user evidence is decision-relevant; elsewhere it is theater.
suggested_improvement: Add a CONSTRAINT SCREEN to META/WHAT for physical or operational systems: enumerate binding constraints (capacity, availability, SLAs, physics) from available data, require explicit capacity math matched to measured outcomes (e.g., cars × capacity vs. surge, single-car wait ≈ observed wait), and classify each user claim by decision-relevance (preference vs. constraint). Add a HOW-verify rule: 'does this alternative change any constraint it does not control?' — an alternative that fails it (app adding zero cars) is rejected on capacity grounds, and a pre-ideation question 'is the fixable thing the experience or the machine?' becomes mandatory.
